fresh_research.topic: BoE Sep.18 2025 provides a matched non-move control for the 2026 QT-duration-supply case
fresh_research.label: HISTORICAL MATCHED CONTROL / SUPPORTS REFINED CAUSAL RULE
observed_facts: On Sep.18 2025 the BoE slowed its annual gilt-stock reduction from £100B to £70B and deliberately skewed active sales away from the long end to about 40% short, 40% medium and 20% long.
The 2025 decision was broadly anticipated: a Reuters poll median expected about £67.5B of annual QT versus the realized £70B.
Immediate market reaction was muted: the 10-year gilt yield was essentially unchanged near 4.622%, while the 30-year yield fell only about 1 bp to 5.423%. Sterling was roughly flat.

By contrast, on Sep.17 2026 the BoE held Bank Rate at 3.75% with a hawkish 6-3 vote split, yet paused all active gilt sales until April 2027, ended long-dated sales, retained £120B of post-2049 gilts to back banknotes, and set a multi-year unwind with £20B annual sales plus maturities.

The 2026 30-year yield fell about 11-12 bp, versus roughly 7 bp for the 10-year and 4 bp for the 2-year, even while markets retained a roughly 75% probability of a November rate hike and nearly four 25 bp hikes through end-2027.

The 2026 headline average unwind pace of ~£46B/year was itself near pre-event market expectations around £50B, and a halt of 20- and 30-year sales had been publicly discussed before the decision. Therefore the entire yield move cannot honestly be attributed to an unanticipated headline QT slowdown.
fresh_research.inference: The stronger causal variable is not scalar QT stock reduction. It is the expectation-adjusted change in market-facing duration supply by maturity and implementation method. A largely anticipated 2025 slowdown/long-end skew produced little immediate long-end repricing, whereas the 2026 package increased certainty that the BoE would stop supplying long-duration gilts to the market, paused all sales for six months and opened a potential direct-transaction route with the DMO. The curve-specific response is consistent with a duration-supply channel, but part of the move may also reflect relief/positioning because several components had been telegraphed.
fresh_research.causal_chain: pre-event expected fiscal/BoE duration supply -> policy announcement changes certainty/timing/maturity/method of market-facing central-bank supply -> marginal absorption requirement changes -> maturity-specific term premium reprices -> long-end yields move relative to front-end policy expectations

matched_control.2025_event: Expected QT slowdown plus fewer long sales; 30y ~-1bp, 10y ~flat immediately.
matched_control.2026_event: All-sales pause + permanent long-end retention + multi-year implementation/direct-DMO option; 30y ~-11/-12bp, 10y ~-7bp, 2y ~-4bp despite hawkish short-rate backdrop.
matched_control.interpretation: Supports expectation-adjusted duration-supply surprise as a better explanatory state variable than gross QT amount.

negative_findings: Do not estimate a stable bp-per-£bn QT elasticity from these two cases.
Do not claim the 2026 long-end sales halt was wholly unanticipated; Reuters reported the possibility before the decision and Deutsche Bank expected it.
Do not attribute the full 2026 gilt rally to QT without controlling for global yields, oil/inflation repricing and positioning.
A Fed May 1 2024 QT slowdown is a poor clean control because Treasury yields also reacted strongly to Powell's rate-path communication; QT and policy-rate surprises were entangled.
fresh_research.supported_method_refinement: For sovereign-duration event studies, compute expected and realized NET MARKET-FACING DURATION SUPPLY by maturity bucket: fiscal issuance + central-bank active sales - maturities/reinvestment/retained holdings/official absorption. Compare the surprise in that schedule with 2y/10y/30y yield changes, policy-path surprise, global-rate controls and positioning. Treat active sales and passive runoff as economically distinct.
fresh_research.decision_support: UK long duration remains WAIT after the already-realized rally. This cycle improves the research model, not an immediate trade thesis.

fresh_research.topic: China Sep.20 LPR hold is a fresh expectation-aligned policy control, not a new easing impulse
fresh_research.label: CURRENT MACRO / EXPECTATION CONTROL
observed_facts: China kept the one-year LPR at 3.00% and five-year LPR at 3.50% for a 16th consecutive month on Sep.20.
All 21 respondents in Reuters' pre-decision survey expected no change.
Credit demand remains weak in property/local-government-linked sectors while policymakers face constraints from narrow bank margins and the wide U.S.-China yield differential.
fresh_research.inference: The decision itself contains little incremental easing information because it matched consensus. Any China-asset repricing should be attributed to subsequent credit/fiscal measures, growth data or trade-policy surprises rather than labeling the unchanged LPR as fresh stimulus.
fresh_research.decision_support: No new China BUY/SHORT thesis from the LPR decision alone.
